title: Елена приходит на ужин с сыном  (Elena Brings Her Son to Dinner)

segments.t: Elena Pavlovna arrives at Claude Monet for dinner, but to Chef Barinov's dismay she brings her son Vasily along so the two men can get along. Vasily immediately sneers at the classic French interior and complains that the restaurant has no entertainment program.
Спасибо, что не в нос.
Вам пришли.
Я не одна.
Я подумала.
Так сказать.
Прошу. Спасибо.
Классическая французская атмосфера.
Ну, нормального дизайнера поленились найти.
И что у вас с шоу программы?
В ресторане люди и едят, они развлекаются.
Когда готовить не умеют, то отвлекают шоу программой.
Ну, мама в ресторане готовить умеет.
Так, так, так.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Спасибо, что не в нос.
'Thank goodness you did not punch me in the nose.' The meaning hinges on 'thank you' working together with 'nose' in spoken Russian.
Вам пришли.
'Your guests have arrived.' Notice how Russian expresses 'for you' and 'have come' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Я не одна.
'I did not come alone.' Vika anchors the line on 'I', while 'one' completes the thought. Dmitry answers right away.
Я подумала.
'I thought it over.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'thought' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Так сказать.
'So to speak.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like this' before landing on 'say'.
Прошу. Спасибо.
'Please, have a seat. Thank you.' The grammar packs 'beg' and 'thank you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Vika answers right away.
Классическая французская атмосфера.
'A classic French atmosphere.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'classic' and finishing on 'atmosphere'.
Ну, нормального дизайнера поленились найти.
'So they were too lazy to hire a decent interior designer.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'normal' in a few short words.
И что у вас с шоу программы?
'And what kind of entertainment show do you have here?' Vika brings out the contrast between 'both' and 'what' in a few short words. Dmitry answers right away.
В ресторане люди и едят, они развлекаются.
'People come to a restaurant to eat, not to watch a circus.' The meaning hinges on 'restaurant' working together with 'to have fun' in spoken Russian.
Когда готовить не умеют, то отвлекают шоу программой.
'When a place cannot cook, they distract guests with a show.' Vika anchors the line on 'when', while 'programme' completes the thought.
Ну, мама в ресторане готовить умеет.
'Well, at mom's restaurant they know how to cook.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'knows how' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
Так, так, так.
